subject: “Are you sure you’re not a Republican?”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Alexandria’s primary opponent certainly doesn’t sound like a Democrat.
#
We recently learned that an ex-Wall Street investment banker launched his campaign to unseat Alexandria in the Democratic primary election.
**This morning, he went on Fox News** — for the second time in a month — to fear-monger about immigration, Alexandria’s policy ideas, and say our movement is ‘trying to turn the U.S. into Venezuela.’
At one point, the Fox anchor asked: **“Are you sure you’re not a Republican?”**
Fighting for climate action, guaranteed healthcare, and a better future for working families is not ‘radical.’ And it’s clear, even to Fox News, that our opponent is not just a ‘moderate Democrat.’
[Wealthy, conservative interests — from Wall Street to AIPAC — want nothing more than to see Alexandria ousted by a multimillionaire who doesn’t even live in her district. Will you make a $5 contribution today to power Alexandria’s reelection campaign so she can keep fighting for all of us?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20240412.W1Jvxw&refcode=em20240412-6180-P_FND_RES_OPP&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=6180%2E2526796%2Emy_11Z)

Alexandria isn’t a former investment banker self-financing her own campaign to preserve the status quo — **she’s a working-class fighter working in Congress to bring real, transformative change to each and every one of us**.
We’re learning more about Alexandria’s opponent and will update you as the primary election gets closer. Whether or not you can give today, thank you for standing with us.
In solidarity,
Team AOC

name: Lizzie Pannill Fletcher
subject: Arizona’s 160-year-old abortion ban
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS
body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/lizzie-reelect-logo-outlined.png]
As you have no doubt seen, the Arizona Supreme Court ruled this week that a 160-year-old abortion ban—a ban issued before Arizona was admitted as a state—can be reinstated following the United States Supreme Court’s Dobbs decision overturning 50 years of Roe v. Wade . If the ban goes into effect, Arizonans can expect what we have already seen in Texas—clinics will close and Arizonans in need, like Texans, will have to travel to other states for reproductive health care of all kinds.
The Arizona ruling came the day after Donald Trump claimed that his position on abortion rights this election year is that abortion should be left to the states to decide. We’ve heard that before. That was the position for years. But make no mistake: Washington Republicans and extremists across the country are pushing for a nationwide abortion ban enshrined in federal law. The Arizona ruling is what it can look like when reproductive freedom is left up to the states, or to Washington Republicans.
Chances are, you aren’t fooled. But it is up to all of us to make sure that people around us understand that Trump’s position on abortion is a political one this election year. In many rooms, he brags about being “the person responsible” for overturning Roe . Just last month, he floated the idea of a national abortion ban. But Trump knows the majority of Americans support abortion rights, and he is more concerned about winning elections than he is ensuring that states can protect or restrict access to reproductive care.
Needless to say, Trump can’t be trusted with these types of high-stakes decisions. Nor can congressional Republicans. Since the Supreme Court overturned Roe , we’ve seen countless efforts to restrict reproductive care—from abortion bans and ordinances prohibiting travel for reproductive care to lawsuits challenging access to the abortion pill and court rulings targeting access to IVF treatment. Time and again, congressional Republicans say there are no real dangers to these forms of reproductive care but then they block bills that would protect the right to travel, birth control, and IVF. We’ve of course seen very real threats to all of those rights—in Texas and across the country.
Trump and Republicans in Congress won’t stand up for our freedom. We must. We do that by speaking out and supporting candidates who will—this year and the years to come. This must be a long-term commitment.
Defending reproductive freedom requires all of us getting involved, and as a dedicated member of our team, I know I can count on you to be a part of our fight. I hope you will add your name here and show you’re committed to our fight for reproductive freedom and equality.

Hi Peter,
During Care Workers Recognition Month, we want to highlight domestic workers like Peggy:
_“19 years ago, when I moved to New York City from the Caribbean, I became a nanny.

Whatever was dished out by my employer – including disrespect – was what I took. When I asked other nannies, they told me that’s just how it was. But I’m not telling a sad story: things are changing!

Nannies are becoming aware that their rights are being violated; they are realizing they deserve the money owed to them. Nannies are willing to stand against these violations.”_
---
All over America, workers like Peggy are standing up and speaking out about their rights — because for too long, they’ve worked under difficult conditions, out of the public eye.
But they can’t do it alone: We need to stand with these workers and raise our voices as well in order to get the attention of our leaders.
**Right now, the Senate is still holding up passage of the expanded Child Tax Credit, and we need your help.**
This expansion would ensure domestic workers (who make an average wage of $13-14 per hour) aren’t excluded from benefits, as many are currently under the minimum required salary.

---
| | Happy Friday!

You might want to bookmark this one...

Because when you find yourself asking,**"how do I know who to vote for?"** these resources will come in handy:
* Here's a scorecard based on the Idaho GOP platform: [Idaho GOP Scorecard](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=3ab81e2248&e=dea908e0fe)
* Check out this one focused on freedom and liberty: [Idaho Freedom Index](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=a6ab155b2d&e=dea908e0fe)
* Take a look at this recent report: [Limited Gov Report](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=2a25c1270e&e=dea908e0fe)
* This site compiles several scorecards: [Think Liberty Idaho Scores](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=617b30ee3e&e=dea908e0fe)

Note, a high "IACI" score is NOT a good thing.

The higher the IACI score, the more a legislator is beholden to corporate interests over individual freedoms. Also, being a member of the "Main Street Caucus" means the legislator leans towards the moderate to liberal side of the Republican party, unlike the Idaho Freedom Caucus, which stands for... well, you know... _freedom._

Cheers,

Brian

**P.S.**

I just caught wind of another $50,000+ bomb the fringe right is dropping on media ads to trash me.

They're desperate to boot me out, fabricating lies nonstop and backing a puppet who'll dance to the tune of bureaucrats, lobbyists, and corporate kingpins. Let's cut to the chase: they're going to outspend me by miles. I'm the regular guy from Nampa fighting for real Idahoans against these power plays. If you want to keep a true voice in the mix, I need your backing.

Every bit helps in this David vs. Goliath battle (and I'm not talking about me vs. the other guy; it's me vs. the system).

Help me stand strong—[click here to contribute](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=49a6d849f9&e=dea908e0fe "fund the fight").

Team, I am incredibly disappointed.
Just earlier this week, the Arizona Supreme Court decided to enforce a law from long before any of us were born, before even our grandparents were born.
They are enforcing a near-total ban on abortion that was originally passed before Arizona was even a state, in 1864, during the Civil War.
No exceptions for rape. No exceptions for incest.
As a father, I am fearful for my daughter. As an Arizonan, I am fearful for the people of my state. And as an American, I am absolutely furious that this has come to pass.
It’s not lost on me that this happened because of the Supreme Court that Donald Trump built, and because the Senate failed to act to protect abortion rights when they had the chance.
It was a dark day, but this is **NOT** over.
If I make it to the Senate, I will do everything I can to pass legislation that will make the protections provided by _Roe v. Wade_ the law of the land — including reforming the filibuster.
I’m a Marine, and I’ll fight alone if I have to. But we’ll accomplish a lot more together. So please, if you’re looking for a way to channel your anger into action, consider supporting my campaign.

clean_body: Earlier this week, the Arizona Supreme Court decided to enforce a law from long before any of us were born | | | Team, I am incredibly disappointed. Just earlier this week, the Arizona Supreme Court decided to enforce a law from long before any of us were born, before even our grandparents were born. They are enforcing a near-total ban on abortion that was originally passed before Arizona was even a state, in 1864, during the Civil War. No exceptions for rape. No exceptions for incest. As a father, I am fearful for my daughter. As an Arizonan, I am fearful for the people of my state. And as an American, I am absolutely furious that this has come to pass. It’s not lost on me that this happened because of the Supreme Court that Donald Trump built, and because the Senate failed to act to protect abortion rights when they had the chance. It was a dark day, but this is NOT over. If I make it to the Senate, I will do everything I can to pass legislation that will make the protections provided by Roe v. Wade the law of the land — including reforming the filibuster. I’m a Marine, and I’ll fight alone if I have to. But we’ll accomplish a lot more together. This is our first real test of 2024: an election year where unprecedented amounts of dark money — from groups like AIPAC and billionaire Trump-acolytes like Jeff Yass — are being spent to unseat The Squad. | **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

# **A Message from the Chairwoman**
---
| | ** _🗳 Early Voting is Open! ✅_**
---
Friends, In-person early voting for the 2024 primary elections is now open! This presents a prime opportunity for all Republicans to step up, cast their votes, and make their voices heard well in advance of the May 7 primary date. While the Biden administration's policies have led to hard times for Americans everywhere, Indiana has been able to keep our ourselves afloat. This is largely due to that fact that we have been fortunate enough to enjoy a Republican supermajority in the Indiana General Assembly, all statewide offices, record number of Republican mayors and about 90% of county officials are Republican. | | [](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/ab1dd88f0e2fd8453947229f28c3afba/ec46d0db78d2113dc3d6b838967d376c/40313)**Governor Eric Holcomb** [announced](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/ab1dd88f0e2fd8453947229f28c3afba/31a2ce170f4db419c3d6b838967d376c/40313) SK Hynix's $3.87 Billion investment for a new semiconductor facility in West Lafayette. This new facility will bring 800 new, high-paying jobs to the area by 2030. **What he’s saying** : “I’m so proud to officially welcome SK hynix to Indiana, and we’re confident this new partnership will enhance the Lafayette-West Lafayette region, Purdue University and the state of Indiana for the long term. This new semiconductor innovation and packaging plant not only reaffirms the state’s role in the hard tech sector, but is also another tremendous step forward in advancing U.S. innovation and national security, putting Hoosiers at the forefront of national and global advancements.” \- **Gov. Holcomb** said in a [press release](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/ab1dd88f0e2fd8453947229f28c3afba/a6ebd0dc940b3b3fc3d6b838967d376c/40313).** **What else happened this week? Holcomb **[attended](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/ab1dd88f0e2fd8453947229f28c3afba/2fe19e4ed409dfe0c3d6b838967d376c/40313) the ribbon cutting ceremony for a new Novartis radioligand facility in Indianapolis. **What he's saying:** "Today we cut the ribbon to celebrate the grand opening of a new [@Novartis ](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/ab1dd88f0e2fd8453947229f28c3afba/3bb36b5a5d42f33cc3d6b838967d376c/40313)radioligand facility in Indianapolis. Holcomb** said in a post on [X](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/ab1dd88f0e2fd8453947229f28c3afba/a3adacc84cf6d9fcc3d6b838967d376c/40313).

**[_Peter, did you see this?! Michelle and Barack Obama just issued a dire warning — and our beloved former first lady said she is terrified about the outcome of this election. _Hey there, folks, it's Black Maternal Health Week and I wanted to pass along this message from my friend and colleague, Lauren Underwood. — Nikki_
* * *
We need to talk about the intersectionality of abortion access and Black maternal health. Ever since the right-wing majority of the Supreme Court struck down _Roe v. Wade_ , millions of women across the country have lost their reproductive freedoms. State houses across the country are either trying or already have banned abortion completely. Our nation’s maternal health crisis was already an urgent concern, and now that millions of women have lost nearly every option for reproductive health care, the crisis has only become worse. And tragically, Black women are facing the brunt of this compounded burden. The CDC reported in 2020 that Black women are three times more likely to die from a pregnancy-related cause than white women. Now, with _Roe v. Wade_ protections gone and a critically low number of abortion providers in our country, this statistic could become even more disproportionate in the future.
Black women deserve to be valued, protected, and supported no matter what decisions they make regarding their pregnancy. This unbearable and unfair trend can only be brought to justice through community action and advocacy.
That’s why I have worked tirelessly to shed light on this problem and use my position in Congress to bring about positive change.

While Republicans only have to defend 10 seats in 2024, Democrats have to defend 23 — and if the GOP flips just two of them, it will deliver Senate control back to Mitch McConnell. Now, experts at FiveThirtyEight are saying that the GOP has a clear path to the majority. As right-wing special interests gear up to pour millions into flipping the Senate, we need to fight back right now. We need more Millennials and Gen-Z folks in the rooms where decisions are being made — and we’re accomplishing that together. The work we are doing together is extremely important to me — and I can’t think of a better way to mark my birthday than to see folks like you joining our fight. I know you get a lot of messages like this but they are an integral part of building our grassroots donor base that enables us to focus as much as possible on electing the next generation of progressive leaders. Thank you!!! David Hogg

Derek — We’re just 3 days away from the filing deadline of _all_ FEC reports — every dollar raised and spent by federal campaigns and PACs from January 1 to March 31 of the 2024 election year. It’s a _huge_ moment for our campaign and its momentum.
It’s also our first mid-month deadline of the new FEC quarter. Before I explain why this deadline is so important to our campaign, **[will you pitch in $10?](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=apr2024_abs_em.I2BRAI&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_MMG_AC90_20240412_PM1_V1_S1&email=&amount=10&t=4&akid=6227%2E5257348%2EUr7Oo3)**

We are building our campaign infrastructure _right now_ to identify and turn out as many voters as possible to win in November. Our fundraising goals have a direct impact on the number of voters we can afford to reach.
Turning out those voters will decide not only whether we win this race, but whether we turn out enough Democrats down-ballot to win the back the House, whether we can support other Democrats to defend the Senate majority, and whether we defeat Trump or see him become, in his own words, a dictator on “day one.”
Your grassroots support powers our campaign, not corporate PACs. That’s gotten under Donald Trump’s skin. He attacks me because he fears that with this national movement of committed, grassroots Democrats working together while the GOP tears itself apart, we may defeat him again.
So Trump, Steve Garvey, the GOP, and their media allies will scrutinize the figures to assess our chance of success, and they’ll question whether we have what it takes to prevail in November.
Derek, I'm prepared to get things done in the Senate. To establish new systems of checks and balances to protect our democracy, eliminate the filibuster, and protect abortion rights. To build an economy that works for everyone, expand access to healthcare, address student loan debt and more.
But achieving these goals hinges on our victory in November — and that's only achievable with your support.

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

Hardworking New Mexicans are suffering from these failures, and they demand new leadership in Washington who will improve, energize, and restore hope to our state and our country. That’s why I’m running for Senate and why over 8,000 voters across all of New Mexico’s 33 counties – nearly 4 times the required amount – have signed the official nominating petition to put me on the ballot. My family’s roots run deep in New Mexico. Our state is blessed with abundant natural resources, cultural diversity, rich traditions, hard-working people, and leading national laboratories and military installations. But sadly, our leaders in Washington and Santa Fe have failed us. I will fight to secure our borders, bring costs down, ease financial burdens on New Mexico families struggling to get by, and ensure America is once again the land of opportunity and freedom. I’m in this fight to win – and with your support, we will get the job done to flip this seat and restore a Republican majority in the Senate! With you in the fight, Nella Domenici Republican for Senate | ABOUT NELLA New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years. Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant. Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans. Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. Follow Nella Online | Paid for by Nella for Senate

Peter,
On Tuesday, the Arizona Supreme Court upheld a pre-statehood law that bans abortions in almost all cases.
This law effectively means an end to abortions in Arizona.
Horrified doesn’t begin to cover how I feel.
This law was passed in 1864. Before Arizona was a state and before women could vote or own property.
Now, it will insert politicians into the most intimate decisions a person will make about their bodies. It will take away rights and freedoms earned by generations of Arizona women. And it will mandate prison time for anyone who helps a woman get an abortion, which could include friends and family as well as medical professionals.
When Donald Trump and Juan Ciscomani say abortion should be left up to the states with a wink and a nod — this is what they mean.
This must be reversed by the people. In Congress, I will fight to restore Roe v. Wade into law, and that starts by defeating Juan Ciscomani, who has voted again and again to restrict abortion access.

Team, This is a longer email about why I’m running for Congress. It means the world to get to share my story with you and tell you why this campaign means so much to me, so I hope you’ll give it a read. **[If you already know you’re with me in our fight for Oregon, can you chip in to my campaign?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/82920284/466709925/-554069173?refcode=em_fr_2024.04.12_b1_as_all-nd&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTUyZGEyYi0wNWY5LWVlMTEtYWFmMC03YzFlNTIwMTcwMzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0iGFiI5wINq_NpcUzTwgiWDCAcSw3oE-gPJUTBDEwrM=) ** As the proud daughter of a Mexican immigrant, I’m a first-generation American. My dad immigrated to the U.S. in 1950, worked in the fields of the Rio Grande Valley, served two tours in Vietnam, and earned his U.S. citizenship.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/82920285/466709926/-554069173?refcode=em_fr_2024.04.12_b1_as_all-nd&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTUyZGEyYi0wNWY5LWVlMTEtYWFmMC03YzFlNTIwMTcwMzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0iGFiI5wINq_NpcUzTwgiWDCAcSw3oE-gPJUTBDEwrM=) He then spent the next three decades as a police officer, and it was this good-paying union job that provided my family a path into the middle class. **While we didn’t have a lot growing up, my family believed that through hard work, better was possible.** It took me seven years to graduate college – and I juggled multiple jobs, from painting houses to pouring coffee – but I put in the hard work and earned that degree. When my daughter was born, I felt the same determination that drove my parents: that I would do everything in my power to shape a stronger, more equitable future for my daughter and her generation. **That’s why I ran for office, and that’s why I’m running for reelection. I’m fighting every day to deliver on the issues that matter most to working families: affordable health care, a fair economy, and an environment that is protected and cherished for generations to come.** But, the reality is that the race here in OR-06 is, once again, shaping up to be one of the most competitive elections in the country. To defend this seat and continue delivering for Oregon in Congress, I’m going to need the support of this grassroots team. When everyone chips in, even just a little, it all adds up. I can tell you from firsthand experience that when folks give what they can, it has a huge impact on our campaign. **I’m asking you to step up and join us today.** **[Please, will you join me in this fight and chip in to my re-election campaign today?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/82920286/466709927/-554069173?refcode=em_fr_2024.04.12_b1_as_all-nd&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTUyZGEyYi0wNWY5LWVlMTEtYWFmMC03YzFlNTIwMTcwMzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0iGFiI5wINq_NpcUzTwgiWDCAcSw3oE-gPJUTBDEwrM=)** | _[CHIP IN $6](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/82920287/466709928/-554069173?refcode=em_fr_2024.04.12_b1_as_all-nd&amount=6&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTUyZGEyYi0wNWY5LWVlMTEtYWFmMC03YzFlNTIwMTcwMzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0iGFiI5wINq_NpcUzTwgiWDCAcSw3oE-gPJUTBDEwrM=)_

This week marked the end of Ramadan, which is normally a joyous celebration for Muslim families throughout the world. But this year, our hearts are heavy as we mourn the more than 33,000 Palestinians killed in Gaza, and 2 million more who have been forcibly displaced and forced to starve. To continue to grow our movement for a ceasefire and human rights, and to ensure Muslim and Arab American representation in government, I want to highlight three Arab American candidates for State Representative in Michigan who I am proud to endorse. Each is committed to ensuring all of our voices are heard, working toward a more just world that uplifts marginalized communities from Michigan to Palestine. As a proud Arab American woman serving in Congress, I know how important it is that our community feels seen, heard, and celebrated by our government. Unfortunately, this month also marks 6 months of genocide against the Palestinian people, with more than 33,000 killed from U.S.-made bombs and ammunition, and 2 million more forcibly displaced and forcibly starved by the Israeli military. That’s why we need more courageous voices that are unapologetically committed to saving lives, no matter faith or ethnicity, by demanding a permanent ceasefire. In Michigan, I’m proud to endorse a number of candidates with diverse backgrounds, and this month in celebration of Arab American Heritage Month, I want to highlight three Arab American candidates for State Representative―each of whom is leading demands for a ceasefire and uplifting the voices of marginalized communities. Because these three candidates have had the courage to speak out for the humanity of the Palestinian people, each is vulnerable to attacks by those who seek to silence us―including by anti-Palestinian group AIPAC, which has pledged to spend $100 million in an attempt to defeat pro-ceasefire candidates running for all levels of office. We've made important strides in demanding representation and ending the systemic erasure of our communities. I've pushed for years to include Arab and Middle Eastern and North African communities in the U.S. Census―instead of requiring us to identify as “white” or “other”―and this year the federal government finally took action to do so. | | | **PRESS RELEASE**

**Drew Johnson announces an impressive $236K fundraising haul in Q1 of 2024**

_This amount is the most raised in Q1 of election year by a GOP candidate in Nevada’s 3 rd Congressional district since 2018_
April 12, 2024 Contact: [info@drewfornevada.com](mailto:press@drewfornevada.com)

(**Las Vegas, NV**) – Today, Republican CD3 candidate Drew Johnson announced a record fundraising haul of $236K in Q1 of 2024.

This amount is more than any Republican CD3 candidate has raised in the first quarter of an election year since 2018. Since announcing his candidacy, Drew has raised $411K.

When asked about his fundraising performance, a member of Drew’s finance committee and top supporter, Lisa Song Sutton, remarked,

“ _I fully support Drew Johnson. He and his wife have been customers of my postal store for many years, and I have come to know them as folks who truly care about the community. Drew is an actual conservative who has an experienced background in policy. We need a well-funded and well-prepared candidate who has been invested in this community and understands the needs of Nevadans to take on Susie Lee in November. Drew is the only person in this race equipped to get his message of secured borders, fiscal discipline, and government accountability directly to the voters and win_.”

Cook Political Report recently changed the rating on the Nevada US Senate race from “Lean-D” to "Toss-Up." CD3 is a top-targeted race by the NRCC, the outcome of the Presidential race, Republicans flipping the Senate, and keeping the House may very well come down to Nevada’s 3rd Congressional district.

You can learn more about Drew Johnson by visiting his webpage at [DrewForNevada.com.](https://DrewForNevada.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=faca3bfedb5031bc3491ebbc8&id=65b898f342&e=fc26432468)

| _Here’s what you missed from this week’s Executive Council meeting→_

**Cinde challenged Frank Edelblut on his disastrous proposed changes to New Hampshire’s education standards that risk the future of New Hampshire’s students.**

Ignoring concerns from teachers about these rules, he is pushing to lower existing minimum standards, remove limits on class size, make many standards optional—not mandatory, and no longer require certified teachers and professionals.

_Many educators are already struggling with their class’s size. How can we expect our students to get a quality education with skyrocketing class sizes that make it harder to learn?_

**[Cinde will never stop fighting for New Hampshire schools, but we need to know our supporters are sticking by her. Will you sign our petition before midnight to show we have a mandate of support?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/82920704/466711300/-1047948903?source=EM_NBI_CW_20240412_PT_1.1_1MO_campaign_na_na_nheducation&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTU0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2YWMwMmQyMC0wN2Y5LWVlMTEtYWFmMC03YzFlNTIwMTcwMzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LbX3vXWTj1KOilxCgX2CpOQeV_wYHNzkdFHJQpNuPnM=&emci=206a7d24-eff8-ee11-aaf0-7c1e52017038&emdi=6ac02d20-07f9-ee11-aaf0-7c1e52017038&ceid=45626166)**

Our education system is a critical pillar of our democracy that serves future generations. We must protect it.

As governor, Cinde will fight to bolster our public schools so that every child in New Hampshire has the opportunity to succeed and prosper—and appoint a new Commissioner of Education who actually believes in public education.

**We cannot allow extremists to carry out their agenda to slowly strip away resources from our public schools and privatize our state education.**

Despite having no background in education, Edelblut was appointed Commissioner of Education and has spent his tenure chipping away at public schools, promoting “indoctrination” programs, and advancing his voucher scheme.

Unlike Edelblut, Cinde knows that public education is the bedrock of our democracy and she believes that we must invest in our neighborhood schools so all students in our state have the opportunity to thrive, no matter their ZIP code.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 4/12/2024
body:
Your daily rundown of REAL news for REAL Coloradans.
Heidi Ganahl introduces the Rocky Mountain Voice, a new conservative news media platform for Coloradans to be the VOICE of your VALUES.
| |
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| Happy Friday! TODAY IS NATIONAL COLORADO DAY! I hope you get out to enjoy this beautiful Colorado sunshine to celebrate. Spring has most definitely sprung. This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, April 12, 2024.
– Heidi Ganahl
---
|
# TODAY'S TOP STORIES
---
[**‘Letter to the American Church’ documentary to show at Cover4 Theater on Sunday, sponsored by Rocky Mountain Voice**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) [THE FORT MORGAN TIMES](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
| [ ](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
A thought-provoking and powerful documentary, “Letter to the American Church,” is set to capture audiences at 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. on Sunday at the Cover4 Theater in Fort Morgan. The event, sponsored by Elevating Life Church and Rocky Mountain Voice, is free and will have two showings. The film, directed by New York Times best-selling author Eric Metaxas, delves into the haunting parallels between the church during the early days of Nazi Germany and the contemporary American church. **[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

[**Sonnenberg qualifies for Republican Party’s primary ballot in 4th District race**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* [Jerry Sonnenberg](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), a former Colorado legislator and county commissioner, has successfully qualified for the Republican Party primary ballot in the competitive 4th District Congressional race.

* Despite a [rejection rate of 45.5%](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for his submitted signatures, Sonnenberg met the signature requirements, submitting 3,155 signatures with 1,719 accepted, surpassing the threshold of 1,500 accepted signatures.

* He will join several other candidates who have also qualified for the ballot through petition, including [Richard Holtorf](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), [Mike Lynch](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), [Lauren Boebert](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), and [Deborah Flora](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Boebert additionally secured her spot on the ballot by earning [40% support from delegates](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) at the assembly.

* The status of ballot petitions for other candidates such as Chris Phelen, Floyd Trujillo, and Peter Yu is still [pending release](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) by the Secretary of State's office.

[**READ MORE**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[**House Republicans welcome homeschooled students to the Capitol**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Approximately [16,000 students in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) claim to be homeschooled, reflecting a broader trend where one in 20 children in America are homeschooled.

* [Colorado Homeschool Day ](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)was celebrated at the Capitol, drawing attention to the importance of empowering families to choose the best education for their children. Minority Leader Rose Pugliese and Rep. Gabe Evans, both Republicans, voiced [strong support for homeschooling](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), emphasizing its benefits such as personalized learning, strong family bonds, and alignment with family values.

* The Colorado House's Republican Caucus issued a[ joint statement ](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)reaffirming their support for school choice and homeschooling, highlighting the importance of familial autonomy and educational freedom. The statement reflects a belief in the principle that families are best positioned to make informed decisions about their children's education, tailored to meet their unique needs and values.

[**READ MORE**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[**Lawsuit alleges Trisha Calvarese, Democratic nominee for 4th CD special election, is ineligible**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Trisha Calvarese, the [Democratic nominee for the 4th Congressional District special election](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in Colorado, is facing a lawsuit alleging her ineligibility due to a state law provision.

* The lawsuit, filed by James "Jim" Glasser, a Castle Rock Democrat, claims that Calvarese was [not affiliated with the Democratic Party](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for the required 12 consecutive months before the convention where she was selected.

* Democratic candidate John Padora has been questioning Calvarese's eligibility, though his campaign [denies funding the lawsuit](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Calvarese maintains that she meets the requirements and plans to fight the challenge.

* The [Colorado Democratic Party supports Calvarese's interpretation of the law](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), stating that there is no residency requirement preventing her from being the nominee.

[**READ MORE**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[**Denver imposes hiring freeze, diverts funds to come up with $90M for illegal immigration crisis**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Denver Mayor Mike Johnston's administration has revised the [city's spending estimate for addressing the illegal immigration crisis](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to $90 million, down from the previous target of $120 million.

* To cover the expenses, Denver has implemented a [hiring freeze on approximately 160 vacant positions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and redirected funds from various sources, including capital funds, technology projects, and service budgets.

* The bulk of the $90 million will be allocated to [housing immigrants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) who arrived in Denver after crossing the U.S.-Mexico border illegally, amounting to around $1,700 per immigrant. Despite the [budgetary strain](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), city officials aim to maintain services without furloughs or layoffs, with plans to resume normal operations for recreation centers and the Department of Motor Vehicles in the coming months.

clean_body: | Welcome to the Indiana Democratic Party's weekly newsletter, The Kernel of Truth. The State Party will provide the most important fact - a kernel of truth - from the week. ** Early Voting Open Across Indiana for May Primary This week, early voting opened all across the state for the May primary election. Voting early is the perfect way to cast your ballot before Election Day, and make sure you’ve done your civic duty. You never know what may come up on Election Day! All registered Hoosiers can view early voting locations and hours for their county at in the voter portal. You can also sign up for an absentee ballot by mail via the portal as well. You can vote at any early voting location in the county in which you’re registered. Make sure to cast your vote for Jennifer McCormick to continue the momentum heading into the summer! Court of Appeals Affirms Abortion Ban Violates Hoosiers’ Religious Freedoms The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld a ruling late last week that allows for a religious exemption to the Republican near-total abortion ban for Hoosiers with deeply held beliefs that their faith allows care when the ban doesn’t.. This ruling is huge, and affirms that the state cannot violate the religious rights of Hoosiers who seek reproductive care for that reason. The ruling also affirms the case as a class action. However, its full impact will be determined by future rulings Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. South Shore trains ran this week between Gary and Michigan City for the first time in over a year. It’s the culmination of the double tracking project led by Hoosier Democrats, including Congressman Frank Mrvan. This project added 14 extra trains per week to Chicago, and updated stations and parking lots across the network. Become a Delegate to the 2024 State and National Conventions Stay up-to-date with the latest news and updates on the 2024 Delegate Selection process. Head to for more information about how to be a part of history next year in Chicago. Rising works with candidates for any level of office (local, state, or federal) in Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, and Illinois as well as staffers and volunteer activists who are helping their local campaigns. # HOUSE REPUBLICANS KILL FISA BILL AND YET ANOTHER FAILURE FOR SPEAKER JOHNSON
---
| | [](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=0&link=98ecac85ffad49dfb5754225e5f37d0b)
---
**A surveillance power authorization bill bit the dust during an April 10th procedural vote because it was against its lack of warrant requirements. This is another failure for Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.), who is already against the wall at the hands of Rep. Marjorie Taylor Green (R-Ga.), who seeks to boot him from the speaker's chair.** This one was from Rep. Laurel Lee, a Republican from Florida, who brought the act titled, “Reforming Intelligence and Securing America.” It would extend the Foreign Intelligence Act’s (FISA’s) Section 702 for five years. Warrantless surveillance power will lapse on April 19th. Normally procedural votes move along nicely with the party lines protecting the proposal from failing. But 19 Republicans partnered with Democrats to kill the bill. The tactic has been frequently used by the GOP to assert pressure on leadership.
| [READ MORE](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=1&link=87d0e70459db4391854353ece5662430)

# SUDDEN SURGE IN LUNG CANCER CASE IN NON-SMOKERS MAY BE DUE TO THIS
---
| | [](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=2&link=56834aabf0dd4b10bce0154373de9981)
---
**A surge in lung cancer cases amongst non-smokers could be down to the radioactive gas radon.** The colorless, odorless gas is the leading cause of lung cancer in non-smokers but the only way to know if you're at risk is to test for it in your home. Around 15 to 20 percent of lung cancer victims have never smoked and are often only in their 40s or 50s.

# WHAT'S BEHIND THE SPATE OF RECENT INCIDENTS ON BOEING PLANES?
---
| | [](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=4&link=8839eb7d4aa14da48ca575c7e3e2a4e8)
---
**Boeing has been in the headlines a lot lately following a series of incidents after the January Alaska Airlines near-miss in which a door panel came off mid-flight.** The episodes point to production and maintenance issues, say experts, who don't see an obvious pattern behind the myriad incidents. The US plane maker has been under scrutiny since January 5, when a Boeing 737 MAX 9 operated by Alaska Airlines made an emergency landing after a fuselage panel blew out, successfully resolving an incident that safety officials say could have been catastrophic.

# COULD WORKING FROM HOME HELP SAVE THE PLANET?
---
| | [](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=6&link=9714fb3bfc634710b5e532ba4002d3c3)
---
**Working from home staff could help cut carbon emissions - at the cost of billions to public transport networks, a new study suggests.** Researchers say more people working from home will help nations reach their climate targets in cutting millions of tons of carbon emissions. But a ten percent increase in remote workers could also cost the transport sector nearly a third of its revenue from ticket fares.
| [READ MORE](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=7&link=8bb1ab14d3514d1bb840d288be8ae628)

# FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS WANT MORE MONEY TO GO AFTER PANDEMIC FRAUD
---
| | [](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=8&link=f65b705843104e3189ed2b7c7c6ce355)
---
**The federal officials tasked with tracking down widespread fraud during and after the COVID-19 pandemic want more time and more money to finish the job.** The Justice Department's COVID-19 Fraud Enforcement Task Force, made up of nearly 30 federal agencies, released its 2024 report on Tuesday. The report details the efforts of the task force in response to fraud involving COVID-19 relief programs. The task force report pointed out that prosecutors have charged more than 3,500 defendants, won more than 400 civil settlements and judgments and that more than $1.4 billion in fraudulently obtained CARES Act funds have been seized or forfeited. The task force has also come up with a new data-driven approach to investigate government fraud.
| [READ MORE](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=9&link=284a73dcb25048fc9a2ac98dbf2efe66)

# FULTON COUNTY DA ASKS APPEALS COURT TO KEEP HER ON THE CASE
---
| [](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=10&link=bba8cf097cb5442eb752c5da493362e4)
---
**Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis wants to move forward with her election interference case against former President Donald Trump.** Willis has asked an appeals court to reject a request from Trump and other defendants to toss her from the case. Willis said Trump and the others simply didn't like the decision of the lower court. "There being no error by the trial court, the present application merely reflects the applicants’ dissatisfaction with the trial court's proper application of well-established law to the facts," Willis and her team wrote in the 19-page brief. "Because the applicants have wholly failed to carry their burden of persuasion, this Court should decline interlocutory review."
| [READ MORE](https://109073.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=8730v7a18lyymive9o&linkid=11&link=38d4c1ab05234a918f872ca5cafcf92c)

But a ten percent increase in remote workers could also cost the transport sector nearly a third of its revenue from ticket fares. | | | FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS WANT MORE MONEY TO GO AFTER PANDEMIC FRAUD | | The federal officials tasked with tracking down widespread fraud during and after the COVID-19 pandemic want more time and more money to finish the job. The Justice Department's COVID-19 Fraud Enforcement Task Force, made up of nearly 30 federal agencies, released its 2024 report on Tuesday. The report details the efforts of the task force in response to fraud involving COVID-19 relief programs. The task force report pointed out that prosecutors have charged more than 3,500 defendants, won more than 400 civil settlements and judgments and that more than $1.4 billion in fraudulently obtained CARES Act funds have been seized or forfeited. The task force has also come up with a new data-driven approach to investigate government fraud. | | | FULTON COUNTY DA ASKS APPEALS COURT TO KEEP HER ON THE CASE | Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis wants to move forward with her election interference case against former President Donald Trump. Willis has asked an appeals court to reject a request from Trump and other defendants to toss her from the case. Willis said Trump and the others simply didn't like the decision of the lower court. "There being no error by the trial court, the present application merely reflects the applicants’ dissatisfaction with the trial court's proper application of well-established law to the facts," Willis and her team wrote in the 19-page brief. "Because the applicants have wholly failed to carry their burden of persuasion, this Court should decline interlocutory review." | | | | ] ] ] ] Email Marketing by [ [DirectIQ ] ](=)

| Peter,

My father, a lifelong public servant, raised my sister and I on his own. As a young child, I saw firsthand the struggles he faced trying to make ends meet while raising two daughters.

Today, too many are struggling to provide for their families. Wages are not keeping pace with the ever-rising costs of living, from housing to healthcare and childcare.

It's why, as Commissioner of Public Lands, I've worked to protect and grow good-paying jobs across the state, including right here in the 6th district.

Through initiatives like my Rural Communities Partnership, we've successfully secured hundreds of millions of dollars, bringing labor and business to the table to create critical jobs in existing and new industries, from _biochar and cross-laminated timber to clean energy, maritime and agricultural investments._

Recognizing the need to create pathways to a stable career, my signature bill expanded funding for apprenticeship programs and job training. And I put in place an apprenticeship requirement on all of our major projects. **That’s why I’ve been endorsed by 27 labor unions in this race – ten times as many as all of my opponents combined.**

name: Becca B.
subject: Being a middle school teacher was the best preparation for running for Congress
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Becca Balint for Vermont
body:
It helped me build a thick skin, learn how to think quickly on my feet, and diffuse arguments among peers.
Peter, it can weigh on you.
Going toe-to-toe with extremist Republicans in Congress.
Battling constant misinformation used to erode our democracy itself.
Watching anti-LGBTQ+ bills pass through the halls of Congress.
I’ve always said that being a middle school teacher was some of the best prep work I could have done before choosing to run for Congress, and I still stand by it. It helped me build a thick skin, learn how to think quickly on my feet, and diffuse arguments among peers.
But some days, this work can be extremely difficult. It’s hard not to feel personally impacted when your humanity and the dignity of those that you love is being put up for debate. Today’s political environment is not for the faint of heart, but I’m honored to be a voice for reason and respect through it all.
Knowing that you’re still standing with me makes all of this work worthwhile, Peter. Can I count on you to chip in $27 or more to my campaign to ensure I get re-elected this November?

|
---
Dear Peter,
My campaign first requested Secret Service protection in May of 2023 with a 63-page declaration showing the many threats that have been made against me.
Despite filing five additional requests, _all have been refused_.
We are currently awaiting responses to our pending requests from both the Secret Service and the White House.
This marks the first time in 55 years that a presidential candidate’s request for protection has been denied.
It's unprecedented in history for a presidential candidate not to receive Secret Service coverage from the administration.
Think about that for a moment—it's a significant deviation from the norm.
---
[](https://www.kennedy24.com/protection-video-donate?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=secret_service_4_12_24_nd1&n=5)
---
Polls, a key factor in determining eligibility for Secret Service protection, show strong support for my campaign.
According to a New York Times/Siena Poll, I'm at 24% in battleground states. An NBC poll suggests 34% of Americans could see themselves voting for me, indicating a base of 50 million Americans rallying behind our vision.
Historically, presidential candidates received Secret Service protection well in advance of the election, regardless of political affiliation—Obama by the Bush Administration, Trump by Obama, and Biden by Trump.
The decision not to grant me Secret Service protection appears to be a strategic move to impact our campaign's momentum and resources. _However, this only strengthens our resolve to push forward and ensure our voice is heard._
The challenges we face, including certain decisions from Secretary Mayorkas and the current administration, highlight the need for vigilance and resilience in our campaign.

Our coalition is building. | | | | | | | Dear Peter, My campaign first requested Secret Service protection in May of 2023 with a 63-page declaration showing the many threats that have been made against me. Despite filing five additional requests, all have been refused. We are currently awaiting responses to our pending requests from both the Secret Service and the White House. This marks the first time in 55 years that a presidential candidate’s request for protection has been denied. It's unprecedented in history for a presidential candidate not to receive Secret Service coverage from the administration. Think about that for a moment—it's a significant deviation from the norm. Polls, a key factor in determining eligibility for Secret Service protection, show strong support for my campaign. According to a New York Times/Siena Poll, I'm at 24% in battleground states. An NBC poll suggests 34% of Americans could see themselves voting for me, indicating a base of 50 million Americans rallying behind our vision. Historically, presidential candidates received Secret Service protection well in advance of the election, regardless of political affiliation—Obama by the Bush Administration, Trump by Obama, and Biden by Trump. The decision not to grant me Secret Service protection appears to be a strategic move to impact our campaign's momentum and resources. However, this only strengthens our resolve to push forward and ensure our voice is heard. The challenges we face, including certain decisions from Secretary Mayorkas and the current administration, highlight the need for vigilance and resilience in our campaign. I want to be clear: my respect for the Secret Service is immense. The issues we face stem from decisions made far above their jurisdiction. Peter,
This week, the Arizona Supreme Court decided to uphold an 1864 law that effectively bans all abortions in our state.
This ruling is a devastating and infuriating blow. The Arizona Supreme Court has decided to throw us back by over a century, adding a barrier between patients, their medical providers, and the healthcare they need.
Let’s be very clear: these attacks aren’t just an assault on our freedoms, it’s an attempt to control us.
This decision does not reflect Arizonans' views on this issue, and we must show them that this November.
This isn’t the first time, nor will it be the last time, that our fundamental rights will come under attack.
That’s why I fully support Arizona for Abortion Access and their efforts to enshrine our fundamental rights into the Arizona Constitution. As your next Congresswoman, I will fight like hell to ensure we codify Roe into federal law.
As Arizona’s most Democratic district, how we vote and turnout can make the difference between codifying abortion rights statewide or reverting to 1864. To protect our fundamental rights, we will need to come together in Arizona’s 3rd Congressional District and fight back. Are you with us? The Arizona Supreme Court has decided to throw us back by over a century, adding a barrier between patients, their medical providers, and the healthcare they need. Let’s be very clear: these attacks aren’t just an assault on our freedoms, it’s an attempt to control us. This decision does not reflect Arizonans' views on this issue, and we must show them that this November. This isn’t the first time, nor will it be the last time, that our fundamental rights will come under attack. That’s why I fully support Arizona for Abortion Access and their efforts to enshrine our fundamental rights into the Arizona Constitution. As your next Congresswoman, I will fight like hell to ensure we codify Roe into federal law. As Arizona’s most Democratic district, how we vote and turnout can make the difference between codifying abortion rights statewide or reverting to 1864. When you hired me as State Treasurer in 2020, I made a promise - now I’m ready to do it again as your next U.S. Representative for West Virginia Congressional District 2.

| [](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=63727a17e2a74692aa8d733e5420cbfe&_e=489iNbNN6GYlsLV-M4DzxPiFY_HlalC7Xcntztj4KxjY_5dkzA_d133KMAhyvgBVs0yQ3Sr5L5s2t7hK5CuTlJAHK6EcQQ9VhK-WM_eGffzxC9Gq6IG-WCJi2PwGaaGVghgbMkEIHL7lMqR6clqNyWQPOQXZ6HYfZbvXqNQU7u980bK8W9vYH39bG-NixGaeYmRWhkSY2c666O83mNPZ9kZ16NuLytGuCraHokLs7IIWdW1Lj3ESm_nSUwvFW4ha3HmJ9Z3J_19ioclEG0stJnO8YwjRUSScX8MX2Cf4HY2kMtQA4IweDIGchKwTyVpC6a2eH9leF-nRNokIMniZ9W8OHtLk6vhiTKMDSq81P0ToFKU88ab5und5Kfc5UMdlFfs4r1R0tongmVt2kXGDig%3D%3D)
---
Fellow American,

I made a promise when you hired me as State Treasurer four years ago. As the next U.S. Representative for West Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District (God willing), I’m ready to do it again.

I promised you that I would get to work for all West Virginians and deliver on our shared goals; goals that will take our state from good to great, and make it the best place for people to live, work, and raise their families.

As I run for a new office, I promise to continue pushing West Virginia to be the best it can be. I’m prepared to fight for you by working to:

* Decrease inflation and put hard-earned dollars back into the pockets of Americans

* Invest in our teachers and children so the next generation can reach their full potential (no more CRT curriculum in schools)

* Put our economy back on track & get folks back to work

* Secure our border to STOP the drugs, crime, and human trafficking poisoning our communities

* Support law enforcement and our military, who work to keep us safe at home and overseas

| | Hi there,
I wanted to pass along my latest Op-Ed in The Coast News, [found here](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=7af0e5455d&e=784f78234b). I’ve got experience dealing with the problems we’re facing that Terra Lawson-Remer refuses to address like homelessness — which under her watch has exploded and now a record amount of people are dying on our streets as a result.
It’s simply wrong and inhumane to let people die on our streets. Under my tenure, San Diego became the only big city in California that actually saw a reduction in homelessness by double digits. Using the same tactics and approach as I did as Mayor will be critical at the County level where I intend to lead starting on Day 1.
Hope we can count on your support! Together, we can turn things around.
# —
# -Kevin

# [My Latest Op-Ed In The Coast News](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=0fa45a8132&e=784f78234b):

# _Tackling Homelessness Requires Political Will. I’ve Done It._

I had the privilege of serving as mayor, and I witnessed firsthand the devastating effects of homelessness on our city’s streets. I have also seen the power of decisive action and compassionate solutions to address this critical issue.
Let me be clear: it is not compassionate to allow people to die on our streets. This is happening in Terra Lawson-Remer’s San Diego, and it’s unacceptable. Homelessness has skyrocketed. Homeless deaths are on the rise. It doesn’t have to be this way.
As we confront the challenges of homelessness throughout San Diego County, I am committed to implementing a multifaceted approach that prioritizes cleanliness, shelter expansion, diversion programs, mental health services, and comprehensive support — all under one roof, just as we did when I was mayor of San Diego.
And it worked.
First and foremost, we must reclaim our sidewalks and public spaces from tent encampments. During my tenure as mayor, I spearheaded efforts to clean up our sidewalks and remove tent encampments, restoring a sense of safety and dignity to our communities.
By implementing proactive enforcement measures through innovative initiatives like the neighborhood policing division, we achieved tangible results — a double-digit reduction in homelessness.
San Diego became the only major city in California to achieve such progress, setting a precedent for effective action. While other cities saw increases, San Diego went in a different direction.
Addressing homelessness requires more than just enforcement. It demands a holistic approach that addresses the root causes and provides meaningful support to those experiencing homelessness.
That’s why I believe it is critical that the county take the lead in increasing shelter beds across the region. Individual cities shouldn’t be bearing the brunt of this crisis alone, throwing taxpayer money away irresponsibly.
It’s the county’s duty to take meaningful action and lead by example. By collaborating with local governments, nonprofits, and stakeholders, we can ensure that every individual experiencing homelessness has access to safe and supportive shelter options.
We must continue to invest in diversion programs and improve mental health services to provide tailored support to those in need. By diverting individuals away from the cycle of homelessness and connecting them with the resources they need to thrive, we can prevent homelessness before it occurs.
Improving mental health systems and expanding access to treatment and support services are essential to addressing the underlying factors contributing to homelessness.
We did all of this under one roof and what was the result? Over 1,000 people were moved away from the streets and into housing.
This is a stark difference from what we’re seeing from the county today, where they’re throwing money at the problem without an actual solution in place that gets people off the streets and into a place of their own. A whole lot of bark, and zero bite.
At the helm of this is Terra Lawson-Remer. She’s had four years to attack the problem at its root, seeing how it was done in other cities like San Diego, but has chosen to sit on her hands. While money has increased, so, too, has the number of homeless individuals living on our streets.
The numbers from 2020 to 2022 increased by 10%, according to the Regional Taskforce on Homelessness, on which Terra Lawson-Remer sits.
It’s only because it’s an election year and Terra Lawson-Remer is on the ballot that she’s emerged with a plan. The reality is that for many homeless San Diegans, it’s too late. Just last year, over 500 homeless individuals perished on our streets, which have become open-air drug markets flowing with fentanyl. It doesn’t have to be this way.
One key component of my plan is to provide individuals experiencing homelessness with a new place to go — all under one roof. By establishing comprehensive service centers that offer a range of support services, including housing assistance, health care, job training, and substance abuse treatment, we can provide a pathway out of homelessness for those who need it most.
These one-stop-shop facilities will streamline access to resources and empower individuals to rebuild their lives with dignity and respect.
In implementing these measures, we must also prioritize collaboration and partnership across sectors. By bringing together government agencies, nonprofits, businesses, community members and homeless service providers, we can harness the collective expertise and resources needed to effectively address homelessness in San Diego.
Together, we can create a stronger, more resilient community where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
As we move forward, let us remember that addressing homelessness is not just a moral imperative — it is a matter of public health, safety, and economic prosperity.By taking decisive action and implementing comprehensive solutions, we can make meaningful progress toward ending homelessness in San Diego once and for all.
_Kevin Faulconer is a former mayor of San Diego and a candidate for the District 3 seat on the San Diego County Board of Supervisors._
_**Read the Op-Ed**_[ _**here**_](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=489c6f1c43&e=784f78234b) _**.**_

I have also seen the power of decisive action and compassionate solutions to address this critical issue. Let me be clear: it is not compassionate to allow people to die on our streets. This is happening in Terra Lawson-Remer’s San Diego, and it’s unacceptable. Homelessness has skyrocketed. Homeless deaths are on the rise. It doesn’t have to be this way. As we confront the challenges of homelessness throughout San Diego County, I am committed to implementing a multifaceted approach that prioritizes cleanliness, shelter expansion, diversion programs, mental health services, and comprehensive support — all under one roof, just as we did when I was mayor of San Diego. And it worked. First and foremost, we must reclaim our sidewalks and public spaces from tent encampments. During my tenure as mayor, I spearheaded efforts to clean up our sidewalks and remove tent encampments, restoring a sense of safety and dignity to our communities. By implementing proactive enforcement measures through innovative initiatives like the neighborhood policing division, we achieved tangible results — a double-digit reduction in homelessness. San Diego became the only major city in California to achieve such progress, setting a precedent for effective action. While other cities saw increases, San Diego went in a different direction. Addressing homelessness requires more than just enforcement. It demands a holistic approach that addresses the root causes and provides meaningful support to those experiencing homelessness. That’s why I believe it is critical that the county take the lead in increasing shelter beds across the region. Individual cities shouldn’t be bearing the brunt of this crisis alone, throwing taxpayer money away irresponsibly. It’s the county’s duty to take meaningful action and lead by example. By collaborating with local governments, nonprofits, and stakeholders, we can ensure that every individual experiencing homelessness has access to safe and supportive shelter options. We must continue to invest in diversion programs and improve mental health services to provide tailored support to those in need. By diverting individuals away from the cycle of homelessness and connecting them with the resources they need to thrive, we can prevent homelessness before it occurs. Improving mental health systems and expanding access to treatment and support services are essential to addressing the underlying factors contributing to homelessness. We did all of this under one roof and what was the result? Over 1,000 people were moved away from the streets and into housing. This is a stark difference from what we’re seeing from the county today, where they’re throwing money at the problem without an actual solution in place that gets people off the streets and into a place of their own. A whole lot of bark, and zero bite. At the helm of this is Terra Lawson-Remer. She’s had four years to attack the problem at its root, seeing how it was done in other cities like San Diego, but has chosen to sit on her hands. While money has increased, so, too, has the number of homeless individuals living on our streets. The numbers from 2020 to 2022 increased by 10%, according to the Regional Taskforce on Homelessness, on which Terra Lawson-Remer sits. It’s only because it’s an election year and Terra Lawson-Remer is on the ballot that she’s emerged with a plan. The reality is that for many homeless San Diegans, it’s too late. Just last year, over 500 homeless individuals perished on our streets, which have become open-air drug markets flowing with fentanyl. It doesn’t have to be this way. One key component of my plan is to provide individuals experiencing homelessness with a new place to go — all under one roof. By establishing comprehensive service centers that offer a range of support services, including housing assistance, health care, job training, and substance abuse treatment, we can provide a pathway out of homelessness for those who need it most. These one-stop-shop facilities will streamline access to resources and empower individuals to rebuild their lives with dignity and respect. In implementing these measures, we must also prioritize collaboration and partnership across sectors. By bringing together government agencies, nonprofits, businesses, community members and homeless service providers, we can harness the collective expertise and resources needed to effectively address homelessness in San Diego. Together, we can create a stronger, more resilient community where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. As we move forward, let us remember that addressing homelessness is not just a moral imperative — it is a matter of public health, safety, and economic prosperity.By taking decisive action and implementing comprehensive solutions, we can make meaningful progress toward ending homelessness in San Diego once and for all. Kevin Faulconer is a former mayor of San Diego and a candidate for the District 3 seat on the San Diego County Board of Supervisors. Read the Op-Ed . subject: Goodrich's ad attacking Spartz "Behavior" is hypocritical
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/spartzforcongress/spartzendorsednra-17375219?e=57d5bacdc3)
---
| |
---
| | Friends,

Chuck Goodrich released an ad this morning attacking Congresswoman Victoria Spartz for “Bad Behavior” using a hit piece based on anonymous sources written by a gossip paper in Washington, DC.

It’s hilarious that Chuck Goodrich attacks Victoria Spartz for her fighting for the American people using footage of her arguing with the Biden Administration. It is true, Victoria Spartz does _not_ sit back and let the liberal establishment win. She fights. She is proud to fight and fight hard because standing meekly invites defeat.

Since Chuck Goodrich prefers to talk about “bad behavior” a quick look at Goodrich’s shady business and political behavior shows a little man drunk on power.

Goodrich and his company try to cover up his **systematic** harassment and abuse. Here are two examples:
1. Administrative Assistant Cindy Chase sued Goodrich’s company for failing to pay overtime and firing her in retaliation for questioning why male employees received remote work privileges while she dd not during COVID-19. (U.S. District Court-Southern District Of Indiana, Case 1:21-cv-1898, Amended Complaint, Filed 9/16/21)
2. Electrician Hillary Lane filed an extensive discrimination lawsuit against Goodrich’s that detailed a toxic work environment where was subjected to sexual harassment and discrimination for pregnancy before she was fired in retaliation for whistle blowing. (U.S. District Court-Northern District Of Alabama, Case 5:21-cv-00864, Complaint, Filed 6/24/21)

No wonder there are rumors of woman and employees being warned to watch out for him.

Goodrich was even _caught covering up_ his behavior.
1. Goodrich’s abusive behavior towards his employees is _described by them_ in Glassdoor reviews. The reviews are so bad, Goodrich is trying to change the results and Glassdoor has a public alert that Goodrich has ordered tampering with the ratings. [https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Gaylor-Electric-Reviews-E403693.htm?sort.sortType=OR&sort.ascending=true&filter.iso3Language=eng](https://spartzforcongress.us4.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c85918f147157cf1c0ccdcf91&id=1b2adf714c&e=57d5bacdc3)

Goodrich has corruptly _abused his power_ as an elected official to enrich his company.
1. Goodrich advanced a bill that would rout nearly $40 million to his company. (_Indy Star_ , 3/14/23)
2. _Indiana’s Fiscal Policy Institute _said Goodrich’s bill had “no proof” that it worked and “lacks important oversight. _(Indiana Capital Chronicle, 3/25/24)_

Chuck Goodrich wants to talk about behavior. Goodrich’s behavior is that of a rich little man, drunk on power and abuses people and the system. He uses his power and money to silence woman and hide his and his company’s behavior. Let’s see if the media will write about his record.

name: All On The Line
subject: A domino effect
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE NATIONAL REDISTRICTING ACTION FUND
body:
Redistricting impacts all of the progressive issues that we care about.
|
---

Friends,
Believe it or not, redistricting impacts all of the progressive issues that we care about, from health care and education to fundamental freedoms like abortion rights. **Gerrymandering can set off a dangerous domino effect — and here’s exactly how it works:**
→ When gerrymandered maps are in place, the outcomes of elections don’t represent the will of the voters.
→ When the will of the voters is misrepresented, legislatures can become lopsided and out-of-touch.
